info.title: Risk Radar
info.description: Real-time transaction risk intelligence. **Advisory**: this service produces a decision (ALLOW / MONITOR / REVIEW / HOLD) with its reasons. It does not block, hold, reverse or freeze anything — enforcement is the caller's responsibility and is documented as such in the contract.

post.description:
FR-006. A naive loop, deliberately (D16: batch/replay is contract-first).

The contract matters more than throughput here: what a caller must be able to
rely on is that replay is idempotent and silent, and that is true of a loop.

One event of any type. Payments are scored; the other types are stored
for the detectors WP-02 adds, and nothing is scored on them yet.
FR-006 for every type: replay is idempotent and silent by default (D8d).

schema.title: Response List Cases V1 Cases Get
Response List Alerts V1 Alerts Get

get.description:
Everything the analyst needs to decide, in one response.

Including — per D24b — the subject's **full transaction timeline across the
correlation window, alerted and un-alerted alike**. Without that, the
incident-level recall claim in §12.3 would be unearned: the analyst would
only ever see the slice that tripped a threshold, and could not tell a
six-transaction extraction from a one-off.

Response Start Review V1 Cases  Case Id  Review Post
Response Add Note V1 Cases  Case Id  Notes Post

post.description:
Record the analyst's verdict.

D13c: these are not a UI status. ``CONFIRMED_FRAUD`` and ``FALSE_POSITIVE``
are analyst-labelled ground truth — the only non-circular labels this system
will ever produce, and the eventual exit from simulator-only training.

schema.title: Response Set Outcome V1 Cases  Case Id  Outcome Post
Response Escalate V1 Cases  Case Id  Escalate Post

post.description:
The customer reported the fraud: start the CBN clocks.

Recorded once. The first report is what the refund clock counts from, so a
second call cannot move it later — correcting it would be rewriting the
moment the bank's obligations began, and belongs in a note, not an update.
The case is pinned to the clock policy in force now.

schema.title: Response Record Report V1 Cases  Case Id  Report Post

post.description:
A moment that stops a clock: acknowledged, receiving bank told, investigation
concluded, customer reimbursed. Each is recorded once, never edited.

Reimbursement pays money back, so it needs ``cases:close`` (a Fraud Ops Lead),
and it needs a concluded investigation that confirmed fraud first.

schema.title: Response Record Milestone V1 Cases  Case Id  Milestones Post

post.description:
Flag the case's customer for at most 24 hours while the bank contacts them.

Risk Radar records the flag; the bank applies it to the customer's BVN.

post.description: The customer was reached. Recorded once, while the flag is active.

schema.title: Response Record Watchlist Contact V1 Watchlist  Flag Id  Contact Post

schema.title: Response Lift Watchlist Flag V1 Watchlist  Flag Id  Lift Post

get.description: Every flag in force now (or recent ones, ``active=false``), soonest to expire first.

schema.title: Response List Watchlist V1 Watchlist Get

get.description: The clock policy in force and the holiday calendar it counts against.

schema.title: Response Clock Policy V1 Clocks Policy Get
Response Assign V1 Cases  Case Id  Assign Post

post.description:
Closing is a FRAUD_OPS_LEAD power, not an analyst one (D12b).

Closing a confirmed-fraud case also promotes its beneficiaries onto the
``KNOWN_MULE`` list, which is the loop closing: the second transfer to a
destination an analyst has already confirmed should not have to re-convince a
model. Recorded in the audit trail with the tokens added, because it is a
control change made by a human and needs to be attributable.

schema.title: Response Close Case V1 Cases  Case Id  Close Post

get.description:
The pile, ordered by what should be worked first.

Ordering happens in Python rather than SQL because the priority formula
combines money, a clock and severity — expressing that in an ORDER BY would
hide the one piece of logic somebody will want to argue with.

post.description:
Hand this analyst the next case and put their name on it.

Assigning on hand-out is what stops two analysts working the same case, and
it is also what makes "cases per analyst per day" a real number rather than
an estimate. A case already assigned to *this* analyst is returned first —
finish what you started before taking something new.

schema.title: Response Next Case V1 Worklist Next Post

post.description:
Record the verdict in one action.

Previously this was three requests: take for review, set outcome, close. An
analyst working forty cases a day should press one key, not three buttons —
and the state machine (D13b) is still respected underneath, with every
transition audited separately.

Closing still requires ``cases:close``. An analyst records the outcome and
the case waits for a lead; a lead does both in the same keystroke.

schema.title: Response Disposition V1 Cases  Case Id  Disposition Post

get.description:
The view a Fraud Ops Lead actually needs, and the one to show a stakeholder.

Not "how good is the model" — that is the QA report. This answers "is the
desk coping": how much is open, how old is the oldest, who is carrying what,
and what proportion of what we raised turned out to be nothing.

post.description:
A step done in the bank's systems, recorded here with its result.

Only the person working the case records steps on it, so the record says who
did what. Risk Radar does not perform the step (D7); it remembers it.

Response Case Links V1 Cases  Case Id  Links Get
Response Overview V1 Metrics Overview Get

get.description:
False alarms per rule and per model, from analyst outcomes (D69d).

Base PRD FR-505: an aggregate false-positive rate hides the one rule that is
drowning the desk. ``by_driver`` answers "which rule, or the model, put
cases in front of analysts, and how often were they right". ``rules``
answers, per rule, how often it fired and how often that became an alert;
for suppressing rules, how often it lowered risk on a customer who had a
confirmed fraud case within a day either side, which is the closest this
system can get to a missed-fraud count without labels on every payment.

schema.title: Response Detection V1 Metrics Detection Get

get.description:
What each alert budget buys, as measured offline (WP-09, D67c).

The figures come from ``ml/budget_menu.py``, not from live traffic: the
fraud a live system misses carries no label, so recall and value detection
can only be measured where the truth is known. Read-only by design.

Response List Rules V1 Admin Rules Get

patch.description:
Enable, disable or retune a rule without a code change.

The change is versioned by creating a new ruleset rather than editing the
active one in place: decisions record the ruleset version that applied
(FR-042), and mutating a version that decisions already point at would make
those decisions unreproducible — quietly, and only discoverably months later.

schema.title: Response Update Rule V1 Admin Rules  Code  Patch

post.description: New version, activated. Never an in-place edit, for the same reason as rules.

post.description:
Entries are supplied as raw account identifiers and tokenised here.

The list never holds an account number — the same one-way boundary as
ingestion (D9c), so an administrator can add a sanctioned destination
without Risk Radar acquiring the ability to resolve one.

post.description:
Promotion is repointing a pointer, audited, with the comparison attached.

Rollback is repointing it back — not a redeploy. ADMIN executes; the metrics
are the authority (D15b).

Walk the chain and report the first break.

Exposed so tamper-evidence is demonstrable rather than asserted: this is the
endpoint to call in the defence, right after showing that the application

BatchIn.title: BatchIn
BatchIn.description:
FR-006. Replayed transactions do not raise alerts unless asked (D8d).

Re-scoring six weeks of history after a model change must not page anybody,
and the default protects that even when the caller forgets.

BudgetConfigIn.title: BudgetConfigIn
BudgetConfigIn.description: D86: the alert budget and how strictly it is paced. Every change is audited with its reason.

CaseActionIn.title: CaseActionIn
CaseActionIn.description: D83: a recommended step done in the bank's systems, recorded with its result.

CustomerReportIn.title: CustomerReportIn
CustomerReportIn.description: D90: a customer reports payments as fraud, whether or not Risk Radar alerted on them.

DeriveThresholdsIn.title: DeriveThresholdsIn
DeriveThresholdsIn.description: D86: solve thresholds from recent traffic; publish only when asked.

DirectiveAckIn.title: DirectiveAckIn
DirectiveAckIn.description: What the bank did with a directive (WP-07, D74). Recorded once.

DispositionIn.title: DispositionIn
DispositionIn.description:
One analyst verdict, recorded in a single call.

``close`` is a request, not a command — the server only honours it if the
caller holds ``cases:close``. An analyst can ask; a lead's ask succeeds.
``followed_recommendation`` is recorded so the desk can later measure how
often the system's advice matched what a human actually decided, which is
the only honest way to find out whether the advice is any good.

IndustryFlagIn.title: IndustryFlagIn
IndustryFlagIn.description: One entry from the industry watch-list, as the bank-side connector received it.

MilestoneIn.title: MilestoneIn
MilestoneIn.description: A moment that stops a regulatory clock. Recorded once, never edited.

PaymentEventIn.title: PaymentEventIn
PaymentEventIn.description: A payment through the envelope: exactly the canonical transaction (§6.1).

ReportIn.title: ReportIn
ReportIn.description: The customer's report that starts the CBN clocks (WP-05, D71).

ReturnIn.title: ReturnIn
ReturnIn.description: D83: an escalated case handed back to the analyst who raised it.

TransactionIn.title: TransactionIn
TransactionIn.description:
One transaction as a channel or switch would present it (§9.1).

Identifiers arrive **raw** and are tokenised before persistence (FR-004): the
boundary is the last place a real account number exists. Callers therefore
send ``customer_id`` and ``account_id``, never tokens — a caller that could
supply a token could also forge one and merge two customers' baselines.

WatchlistPlaceIn.title: WatchlistPlaceIn
WatchlistPlaceIn.description: A temporary watch-list flag on the case's customer (WP-06, D73).
